verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. `doubleAverage` is the composite in the order ⟨⟨·⟩_θ⟩_Y and unfolds to ∫_0^1∫_0^1 [(∫_0^{2π} F(Y,θ)dθ)/(2π)] dx dy, which is the paper's displayed iterated integral (1/2π)∫_{T²}∫_0^{2π} F dϑ dY with the same constant and the same order of integration. Two reformulations: (i) `doubleAverage` takes no slow arguments — the dependence on (r,z,t) is carried by the caller, and `meanBar_symmetricCovariance` is the form with the slow point x held fixed, equating ⟨⟨·⟩_θ⟩_Y (torus average of the angular covariance) with `doubleAverage` for the symmetric-covariance integrand; (ii) the asserted equality with the reversed order ⟨⟨F⟩_Y⟩_θ is not stated as a lemma about these two operators, but follows from `torusMean_intervalIntegral` with a = 0, b = 2π applied to g(ϑ,Y) = F(r,ϑ,z,t,Y) and divided by 2π, for F continuous in (ϑ,Y) jointly; I did not find a declaration asserting that commutation for `squareAverage ∘ angularMean` directly.
